clips.title: The story
paras: Hammerfall recounts the tragic fall of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer during the liberation of an Alliance internment camp in the Arathi Highlands. Through the grief-stricken memories of Gor'mul, travelers learn how the camp was freed and why the stronghold bears its solemn name.

Hammerfall was once a grim Alliance internment camp where captive orcs were kept behind wood and steel after the Second War. That changed when young Thrall and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer launched an assault to shatter the enclosures and free their kin. Though the raid succeeded in freeing many captives and bringing down the camp's defenses, it ended in tragedy when Doomhammer was struck from behind by a mounted lance, dying on the very soil where the Horde settlement now stands.

Not every captive found freedom on that fateful day. In the chaos of battle and the tremors of the earth, an orc named Gor'mul watched the legendary Warchief fall and lost all will to fight. Left behind as his brethren fled, Gor'mul spent years wandering the highlands in directionless grief. Even now that the Horde has reclaimed the site as a fortified base, the memory of that cowardly strike continues to haunt those who survived it.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: It is still clear to me, like yesterday... So many years without hope, with wood and steel to bind me to this terrible place. Then finally, finally! There was the Warchief. Doomhammer in his midnight plate, his warhammer held high.

It was... Too terrible... That the blow of a coward would strike down our greatest hero. From behind he charged on his horse, and then his lance ran him through... I fell to my knees. What hope was there? What hope is there...

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah, Gor'mul you speak of. Yes, from what he says, it seems he has never recovered from the death of Doomhammer.

Gor'mul was a captive here when Thrall and Orgrim fought to free the camp, but as the earth shook and our brethren escaped, he was left behind. He wandered alone and lost for years without direction or hope, until we returned to establish ourselves here in Hammerfall.
